items.informal_name: Total Degree of Renamed Multivariate Polynomial is Non-Increasing
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : σ → τ) (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  ((MvPolynomial.rename f) p).totalDegree ≤ p.totalDegree
items.informal_description: For any function $ f : \sigma \to \tau $ and any multivariate polynomial $ p \in R[\sigma] $ over a commutative semiring $ R $, the total degree of the polynomial obtained by renaming variables according to $ f $ satisfies $ \text{totalDegree}(\text{rename } f\, p) \leq \text{totalDegree}(p) $.

items.informal_name: Degree Bound in Coefficients via Fin(n+1) Equivalence
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommSemiring R] {n : ℕ} (p : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R) (j : Fin n) (i : ℕ),
  MvPolynomial.degreeOf j (((MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv R n) p).coeff i) ≤ MvPolynomial.degreeOf j.succ p
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $ p $ over $ \text{Fin}(n+1) $, any $ j \in \text{Fin}(n) $, and any natural number $ i $, the degree of the variable $ j $ in the $ i $-th coefficient of the polynomial obtained by applying the algebra equivalence $ \text{finSuccEquiv} $ to $ p $ is less than or equal to the degree of the variable $ j.\text{succ} $ in $ p $. This equivalence maps variables indexed by $ \text{Fin}(n+1) $ to a polynomial ring in one variable with coefficients in multivariate polynomials over $ \text{Fin}(n) $, preserving algebraic structure while bounding variable degrees in coefficients.

items.informal_name: Non-Increasing Multiset Degrees Under Ring Homomorphism in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S : Type v} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] {p : MvPolynomial σ R} [inst_1 : CommSemiring S]
  {f : R →+* S}, ((MvPolynomial.map f) p).degrees ≤ p.degrees
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ S $ and a ring homomorphism $ f : R 	o S $, the multiset of variable degrees of the polynomial obtained by applying $ f $ to coefficients of $ p $ is a submultiset of the multiset of variable degrees of $ p $. This means every variable in the mapped polynomial appears with multiplicity no greater than in the original polynomial.

items.informal_name: Degree Preservation under Fin(n+1) to Polynomial Ring Equivalence
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommSemiring R] {n : ℕ} {f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R},
  f ≠ 0 → ((MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv R n) f).degree = ↑(MvPolynomial.degreeOf 0 f)
items.informal_description: For a nonzero multivariate polynomial $ f $ over $ \text{Fin}(n+1) $, the degree of the equivalent polynomial obtained via the algebra equivalence to the polynomial ring in one variable with coefficients in multivariate polynomials over $ \text{Fin}(n) $ is equal to the total degree of $ f $ in the variable indexed by $ 0 $. This equivalence is constructed by renaming variables through the bijection $ \text{Fin}(n+1) \simeq \text{Option}(\text{Fin}(n)) $, mapping the new variable to the outer polynomial's indeterminate.

items.informal_name: Degrees of Renamed Multivariate Polynomial are Subset of Mapped Original Degrees
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : σ → τ) (φ : MvPolynomial σ R),
  ((MvPolynomial.rename f) φ).degrees ⊆ Multiset.map f φ.degrees
items.informal_description: For a multivariate polynomial $\varphi$ over a commutative semiring $R$ with variables indexed by $\sigma$, and a function $f : \sigma \to \tau$, the multiset of variables in the renamed polynomial $\varphi^f$ (obtained by substituting variables via $f$) satisfies $\mathrm{degrees}(\varphi^f) \subseteq f_*(\mathrm{degrees}(\varphi))$, where $f_*$ denotes the multiset image operation that applies $f$ to each element of the original variable multiset.

items.informal_name: Natural Degree Under FinSucc Equivalence Equals Zeroth Variable Degree
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommSemiring R] {n : ℕ} (f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R),
  ((MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv R n) f).natDegree = MvPolynomial.degreeOf 0 f
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $ f $ with variables indexed by $ \text{Fin}(n+1) $, the natural degree of the polynomial obtained via the finSuccEquiv transformation is equal to the total degree of $ f $ in the zeroth variable. Symbolically, $ \text{natdeg}(\text{finSuccEquiv}(f)) = \text{degreeOf}(0, f) $.

items.informal_name: Total Degree Inequality for Coefficients in Fin(n+1) Polynomial Equivalence
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommSemiring R] {n : ℕ} (f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R) (i : ℕ),
  ((MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv R n) f).coeff i ≠ 0 →
    (((MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv R n) f).coeff i).totalDegree + i ≤ f.totalDegree
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $ f $ over $ \text{Fin}(n+1) $ with coefficients in a commutative semiring $ R $, and for any natural number $ i $ such that the $ i $-th coefficient of the algebra equivalence $ \text{finSuccEquiv}(R, n, f) $ is nonzero, the total degree of this coefficient polynomial plus $ i $ is less than or equal to the total degree of $ f $. This reflects the degree preservation property under the variable-renaming equivalence between $ R[\text{Fin}(n+1)] $ and $ R[\text{Fin}(n)][X] $.

items.informal_name: Algebra Equivalence for Multivariate Polynomials with Option-Indexed Variables
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : DecidableEq σ] (a : σ) (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  MvPolynomial.degreeOf a p =
    ((MvPolynomial.optionEquivLeft R { b // b ≠ a })
        ((MvPolynomial.rename ⇑(Equiv.optionSubtypeNe a).symm) p)).natDegree
items.informal_description: There exists an algebra equivalence between the ring of multivariate polynomials over a commutative semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \text{Option } \sigma $, and the polynomial ring in one variable whose coefficients are multivariate polynomials over $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $. This equivalence maps variables corresponding to $ \text{none} $ to the outer polynomial indeterminate and variables corresponding to $ \text{some } s $ to coefficients in the inner multivariate polynomial ring, with the inverse given by variable substitution.

items.type:

This equivalence is constructed by renaming variables through the bijection $ \text{Fin}(n+1) \simeq \text{Option}(\text{Fin}(n)) $, mapping the new variable to the outer polynomial's indeterminate.

items.informal_name: Natural Degree Under FinSucc Equivalence Equals Zeroth Variable Degree
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommSemiring R] {n : ℕ} (f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R),
  ((MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv R n) f).natDegree = MvPolynomial.degreeOf 0 f
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $ f $ with variables indexed by $ \text{Fin}(n+1) $, the natural degree of the polynomial obtained via the finSuccEquiv transformation is equal to the total degree of $ f $ in the zeroth variable. Symbolically, $ \text{natdeg}(\text{finSuccEquiv}(f)) = \text{degreeOf}(0, f) $.

items.informal_name: Algebra Equivalence for Multivariate Polynomials with Option-Indexed Variables
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : DecidableEq σ] (a : σ) (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  MvPolynomial.degreeOf a p =
    ((MvPolynomial.optionEquivLeft R { b // b ≠ a })
        ((MvPolynomial.rename ⇑(Equiv.optionSubtypeNe a).symm) p)).natDegree
items.informal_description: There exists an algebra equivalence between the ring of multivariate polynomials over a commutative semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \text{Option } \sigma $, and the polynomial ring in one variable whose coefficients are multivariate polynomials over $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $. This equivalence maps variables corresponding to $ \text{none} $ to the outer polynomial indeterminate and variables corresponding to $ \text{some } s $ to coefficients in the inner multivariate polynomial ring, with the inverse given by variable substitution.

items.informal_name: Degree Bound in Coefficients via Fin(n+1) Equivalence
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommSemiring R] {n : ℕ} (p : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R) (j : Fin n) (i : ℕ),
  MvPolynomial.degreeOf j (((MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv R n) p).coeff i) ≤ MvPolynomial.degreeOf j.succ p
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $ p $ over $ \text{Fin}(n+1) $, any $ j \in \text{Fin}(n) $, and any natural number $ i $, the degree of the variable $ j $ in the $ i $-th coefficient of the polynomial obtained by applying the algebra equivalence $ \text{finSuccEquiv} $ to $ p $ is less than or equal to the degree of the variable $ j.\text{succ} $ in $ p $. This equivalence maps variables indexed by $ \text{Fin}(n+1) $ to a polynomial ring in one variable with coefficients in multivariate polynomials over $ \text{Fin}(n) $, preserving algebraic structure while bounding variable degrees in coefficients.

items.informal_name: Injective Renaming Preserves Variable Degree in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] {p : MvPolynomial σ R} {f : σ → τ},
  Function.Injective f → ∀ (i : σ), MvPolynomial.degreeOf (f i) ((MvPolynomial.rename f) p) = MvPolynomial.degreeOf i p
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $ p $ over a commutative semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $, and for any injective function $ f : \sigma \to \tau $, the total degree of the variable $ f(i) $ in the renamed polynomial $ \operatorname{rename}(f, p) $ equals the total degree of the variable $ i $ in the original polynomial $ p $. Symbolically, $ \deg_{f(i)}(\operatorname{rename}(f, p)) = \deg_i(p) $.

items.informal_name: Algebra Equivalence Between Multivariate Polynomials Over Option σ and Polynomials in One Variable with Multivariate Coefficients
items.type:

  f ≠ 0 → ((MvPolynomial.optionEquivLeft R σ) f).degree = ↑(MvPolynomial.degreeOf none f)
items.informal_description: There exists an algebra equivalence between the ring of multivariate polynomials with variables indexed by $\text{Option } \sigma$ and coefficients in a commutative semiring $R$, and the polynomial ring in one variable whose coefficients are multivariate polynomials over $R$ with variables indexed by $\sigma$. This equivalence maps variables in $\text{Option } \sigma$ to either the indeterminate of the outer polynomial ring (for the $\text{none}$ case) or coefficients in the inner multivariate polynomial ring (for the $\text{some } s$ cases), with the inverse given by substituting renamed variables. For any nonzero polynomial $f$, the degree of the transformed polynomial equals the total degree of $f$ in the $\text{none}$ variable.

items.type:
